Arctic sea ice has declined in extent and thickness over the satellite era as the Arctic has warmed about twice as fast as the global mean (Arctic amplification). The IUCN and Arctic scientists treat loss of sea-ice hunting habitat as the primary long-term threat to the species. That snapshot does not cancel the physical dependence on ice or projections of increased fasting and reduced cub survival as ice-free seasons lengthen, especially in southern parts of the range. Conservation hunting quotas and pollution are additional pressures, but they do not make sea-ice loss irrelevant. There is no scientific basis for the claim that polar bears are thriving because of chemtrails or that global warming is a hoax because one subpopulation increased.
